div.div: SSR is not free. The server renders, sends HTML, then React re-renders the whole tree in the browser to attach event handlers. Until that finishes, the page is a picture.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 348px; height: 1px; padding-top: 403px; margin-left: 430px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: var(--dg-bad-fg);

display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: 'IBM Plex Sans',-apple-system,BlinkMacSystemFont,'Segoe UI',Roboto,sans-serif; color: var(--dg-bad-fg); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div: A hydration mismatch — Date.now(), window, a random id — makes React discard the server HTML for that subtree and re-render it. You paid for SSR and got CSR.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 756px; height: 1px; padding-top: 509px; margin-left: 40px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: var(--dg-warn-fg);

display: inline-block; font-size: 12px; font-family: 'IBM Plex Sans',-apple-system,BlinkMacSystemFont,'Segoe UI',Roboto,sans-serif; color: var(--dg-warn-fg); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div: Pick by who owns the content and how fresh it must be. "SSR is faster" is wrong — SSR moves work, and hydration adds some back.
